title: Base change compatibility of the direct-image counit
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] whose structure morphism is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X$ be a $k$-rational point [def-pc-rational-point]. Assume that for every scheme $T$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ the module category on $X_T$ has injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a morphism $i:T'\to T$ over $k$ and an object $\mathcal L\in F(T)$ of the invertible-direct-image subfunctor [def-pc-f-subfunctor] of the normalized Picard functor [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor], the pullback along the induced base-change map of the adjunction counit $f_T^*f_{T,*}\mathcal L\to\mathcal L$ is isomorphic as an arrow to the counit $f_{T'}^*f_{T',*}(i_X^*\mathcal L)\to i_X^*\mathcal L$ for the pulled-back object.

proof.text: Use the complete adopted proof in ZeroScheme.lean. Put sT and sTprime equal to the base-changed structure maps, iPrime = baseChangeMap, d equal to the skeleton representative of the given Picard class, and alpha equal to the canonical square of ordinary pullback functors. Its mate beta is the ordinary direct-image base-change map. IsInvertibleDirectImage.map_of_isProper, the subfunctor assertion of [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor], shows that the pulled-back class is still in F. Together with rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf and the skeleton representative isomorphism this makes both source and target of beta invertible.

Apply [lem-pc-invertible-morphism-iso-on-residue-fibres] to beta. For a point tprime, let p: Spec kappa(tprime) -> Tprime be its residue-field map. Choose a free generator of fT_*d on an affine neighbourhood of i(tprime). The composite p followed by i lands in this neighbourhood. If p^*beta were zero, pullback composition and the mate counit identity would imply that the counit of d pulled back along the composite baseChangeMap were zero. This contradicts [lem-pc-counit-nonzero-after-affine-base-change]. The affine source Spec kappa(tprime) has nontrivial global functions, so all hypotheses of that theorem hold; the flatness and local finite presentation of the structure morphism that it needs come from smoothness [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Thus beta is invertible.

The canonical square alpha is an isomorphism on every object, since it is built from pullbackComp and pullbackCongr. Apply the proved categorical Adjunction.arrowIsoMapCounit (MatesArrow.lean), whose square is exactly Mathlib mateEquiv_counit followed by cancellation of alpha, to get an arrow isomorphism to the counit at iPrime^*d. Finally compose with Arrow.isoMk using the inverse fromSkeletonToSkeletonIso on iPrime^*d; counit naturality gives its commuting square. This is the full existing Lean argument at ZeroScheme.lean lines 197-281 and uses no derived-base-change comparison.
